q: Cathode rays are fast moving ____ emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube.
e: Cathode rays are fast electrons leaving the cathode. Cathode rays are fast moving electrons emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube.

q: They were discovered while studying the electric discharge through gases at ____ pressure.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. They were discovered while studying the electric discharge through gases at low pressure.

q: Electric discharge first occurs at about ____ Hg.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Electric discharge first occurs at about 20mm Hg.

q: As the pressure is reduced further, at very low pressure(~0.01 mm Hg) glass behind the positive electrode(____) is observed to glow.
e: The discharge that revealed cathode rays is a low-pressure gas discharge. As the pressure is reduced further, at very low pressure(~0.01 mm Hg) glass behind the positive electrode(anode) is observed to glow.

q: Cathode rays were first observed in 1869 by Julius Plucker and Johann Hittorf, and were named in 1876 by ____ as cathode rays.
e: Plucker and Hittorf first saw the rays in 1869. Cathode rays were first observed in 1869 by Julius Plucker and Johann Hittorf, and were named in 1876 by Eugen Goldstein as cathode rays.

q: In 1897, British physicist ____ showed that cathode rays composed of a previously unknown negatively charged particle, which was later named the electron.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In 1897, British physicist Joseph John Thomson showed that cathode rays composed of a previously unknown negatively charged particle, which was later named the electron.

q: He measured the charge to mass ratio (e/m) of electron and found to be ____.
e: Thomson's e/m is about 1.76 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹. With Millikan's e you get the electron mass. He measured the charge to mass ratio (e/m) of electron and found to be -1.759× 10^11Ckg^-1.

q: Combining with the charge of the electron $-1.602\times 10^{-19}\text{C}$ (measured by ____ in 1906), the mass of the electron is $9.107\times 10^{-31}\text{kg}$.
e: Millikan measured e. Combined with e/m that gives the electron mass, about 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. Combining with the charge of the electron -1.602× 10^-19C (measured by Robert Andrews Millikan in 1906), the mass of the electron is 9.107× 10^-31kg.

q: From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays travel in ____ lines.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays travel in straight lines.

q: From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays have ____ and kinetic energy.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays have momentum and kinetic energy.

q: From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can be deflected by both electric and ____ fields.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can be deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.

q: From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can ____ the gases through which they pass.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can ionize the gases through which they pass.

q: From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can produce ____.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. From the experiment with cathode rays it is found that cathode rays can produce fluorescence.

q: The cathode ray tube(CRT) is a vacuum tube that contains an electron gun, a deflection system and a ____ screen, and is used to display images.
e: A CRT is a vacuum tube with an electron gun, deflection plates, and a fluorescent screen. The cathode ray tube(CRT) is a vacuum tube that contains an electron gun, a deflection system and a fluorescent screen, and is used to display images.

q: Before late 2000 AD, CRTs are widely used in cathode ray oscilloscopes (____), television sets and computer monitors.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Before late 2000 AD, CRTs are widely used in cathode ray oscilloscopes (CROs), television sets and computer monitors.

q: Since then CRTs have been largely superseded by newer flat-panel display technologies such as liquid crystal display(LCD), plasma display, and organic light-emitting diode (____) displays.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Since then CRTs have been largely superseded by newer flat-panel display technologies such as liquid crystal display(LCD), plasma display, and organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays.

q: Cathode rays are ____.
e: Cathode rays are invisible electrons. You see them only when they make glass or a screen fluoresce. Cathode rays are invisible.

q: However, when cathode rays struck the glass wall of a tube or a fluorescent screen they can cause a glow called ____.
e: A CRT is a vacuum tube with an electron gun, deflection plates, and a fluorescent screen. However, when cathode rays struck the glass wall of a tube or a fluorescent screen they can cause a glow called fluorescence.

q: X-rays are electromagnetic waves like light, but their wavelengths are much ____ than those of light.
e: By the late 1800s light was known to be an electromagnetic wave. X-rays are electromagnetic waves like light, but their wavelengths are much shorter than those of light.

q: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in ____ while experimenting with cathode rays.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode rays.

q: Because he did not know what the rays were, he called them X-rays, meaning ____ rays.
e: Because he did not know what the rays were, he called them X-rays, meaning unknown rays. The name used here is unknown.

q: Later experiments revealed that X-rays are electromagnetic waves which have a wavelength in the range of ____ to 10 nanometre (nm).
e: By the late 1800s light was known to be an electromagnetic wave. Later experiments revealed that X-rays are electromagnetic waves which have a wavelength in the range of 0.01 to 10 nanometre (nm).

q: They are shorter in wavelength than ultraviolet (UV) rays and longer than ____ rays.
e: They are shorter in wavelength than ultraviolet (UV) rays and longer than gamma rays. Gamma is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays of energy about 0.1 to 10 keV (wavelength 10 to 0.10 nm) are classified as ____ X-rays.
e: X-rays of energy about 0.1 to 10 keV (wavelength 10 to 0.10 nm) are classified as soft X-rays. Soft is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays of energy about 10 to 100keV(wavelength 0.10 to 0.01nm) are classified as ____ X-rays, due to their penetrating abilities.
e: X-rays of energy about 10 to 100keV(wavelength 0.10 to 0.01nm) are classified as hard X-rays, due to their penetrating abilities. Hard is what this statement is using.

q: 1 electron volt (eV) = ____ J is an energy unit used in atomic and nuclear physics.
e: 1 electron volt (eV) = 1.602× 10^-19 J is an energy unit used in atomic and nuclear physics. Leave the relation as 1.602× 10^-19.

q: An X-ray tube consists of a cathode and a target (____).
e: An X-ray tube consists of a cathode and a target (anode). Anode is what this statement is using.

q: A high potential difference (about 10-100 kV) is applied between target and cathode to ____ electrons emitted from the cathode.
e: A high potential difference (about 10-100 kV) is applied between target and cathode to accelerate electrons emitted from the cathode. Accelerate is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons strike the target which is made of a high dense material such as ____.
e: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons strike the target which is made of a high dense material such as tungsten. Tungsten is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays have no charge, cannot be deflected by both electric and ____ fields.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. X-rays have no charge, cannot be deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.

q: They travel through vacuum with the speed of ____.
e: They travel through vacuum with the speed of light. Light is what this statement is using.

q: They have high ____ power.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. They have high penetrating power.

q: Hence, thick dense shielding, such as high density concrete or ____ is necessary to protect against X-rays.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. Hence, thick dense shielding, such as high density concrete or lead is necessary to protect against X-rays. Lead is what this sentence is naming.

q: Soft tissue(like organs and skin) cannot absorb the X-rays; however high density materials(such as ____) absorb X-rays.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. Soft tissue(like organs and skin) cannot absorb the X-rays; however high density materials(such as bone) absorb X-rays. Bone is what this sentence is naming.

q: X-rays can cause ____ by stripping electrons from the atoms and can cause biological effects.
e: X-rays can cause ionization by stripping electrons from the atoms and can cause biological effects. Ionization is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays consist of high energy ____ which are energy packets of electromagnetic wave.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. X-rays consist of high energy photons which are energy packets of electromagnetic wave.

q: soft X-rays (low penetrating power) are used to take X-ray photographs of some parts of ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Soft X-rays (low penetrating power) are used to take X-ray photographs of some parts of human body.

q: Hard X-rays (high penetrating power) are used to destroy ____ cells.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Hard X-rays (high penetrating power) are used to destroy cancer cells.

q: X-rays are used in industries for finding defects in welded joints and metal ____.
e: X-rays are used in industries for finding defects in welded joints and metal castings. Castings is what this statement is using.

q: Since X-rays can exhibit wave nature, they are used to determine the structure of ____.
e: Since X-rays can exhibit wave nature, they are used to determine the structure of crystals. Crystals is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays are also used in security systems to reveal hidden unlawful materials (such as weapons and ____).
e: X-rays are also used in security systems to reveal hidden unlawful materials (such as weapons and drugs). Drugs is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays can be classified as two types: (i) characteristic X-rays (intense sharp lines) and (ii) continuous X-rays (or) ____ X-rays.
e: X-rays can be classified as two types: (i) characteristic X-rays (intense sharp lines) and (ii) continuous X-rays (or) white X-rays. White is what this statement is using.

q: When a high energy electron emitted from the cathode bombard the target material, it may knock an electron in the ____-shell of an atom completely out of its orbit.
e: When a high energy electron emitted from the cathode bombard the target material, it may knock an electron in the inner-shell of an atom completely out of its orbit. Inner is what this statement is using.

q: When outer-shell electrons, having higher energy, fill the vacancy in the inner shell, the energy is released in the form of ____.
e: When outer-shell electrons, having higher energy, fill the vacancy in the inner shell, the energy is released in the form of X-rays. X-rays is what this statement is using.

q: These X-rays are called characteristic X-rays because they have specific energies characteristic of the element used as the ____.
e: These X-rays are called characteristic X-rays because they have specific energies characteristic of the element used as the target. The name used here is target.

q: When an electron striking the target passes through the atoms of the target material, it will suffer a retarding force in the ____ field of the nuclei of the target.
e: When an electron striking the target passes through the atoms of the target material, it will suffer a retarding force in the Coulomb field of the nuclei of the target. Coulomb is what this statement is using.

q: When this occurs, the electron will lose some of its ____ energy and the energy is released in the form of X-rays.
e: When this occurs, the electron will lose some of its kinetic energy and the energy is released in the form of X-rays. Kinetic is what this statement is using.

q: Continuous X-rays are also called ____ radiation (braking radiation) according to the phenomenon they are produced.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. Continuous X-rays are also called bremsstrahlung radiation (braking radiation) according to the phenomenon they are produced.

q: Rutherford's model states that an atom has a central ____ and an electron or electrons revolve around it.
e: Rutherford's scattering showed a tiny positive nucleus. Rutherford's model states that an atom has a central nucleus and an electron or electrons revolve around it.

q: However, according to electromagnetic theory, accelerating charged particles, i.e., the orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally they will collapse into the ____.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. However, according to electromagnetic theory, accelerating charged particles, i.e., the orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally they will collapse into the nucleus.

q: In order to overcome this drawback of Rutherford's atomic model, ____ proposed a new model.
e: Rutherford's scattering showed a tiny positive nucleus. In order to overcome this drawback of Rutherford's atomic model, Niels Bohr proposed a new model.

q: Bohr postulated that in an atom, an electron can move only in allowed ____ orbits.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. Bohr postulated that in an atom, an electron can move only in allowed circular orbits.

q: If an electron is moving in such an orbit, it does not absorb(or) emit ____.
e: If an electron is moving in such an orbit, it does not absorb(or) emit radiation. Radiation is what this statement is using.

q: The atom can exist in certain stable states with a definite total ____.
e: The atom can exist in certain stable states with a definite total energy. Energy is what this statement is using.

q: An electron revolves around the nucleus in circular orbits with angular momentum L which is an integral multiple of ____.
e: Angular momentum is L = Iω. An electron revolves around the nucleus in circular orbits with angular momentum L which is an integral multiple of h/2π.

q: This postulate is the concept of angular momentum ____.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. This postulate is the concept of angular momentum quantization.

q: An electron can undergo transition from an orbit to another by absorbing (or) emitting energy which is equal to the energy ____ between the two states.
e: An electron can undergo transition from an orbit to another by absorbing (or) emitting energy which is equal to the energy difference between the two states. Difference is what this statement is using.

q: An electron of charge e and mass m moving in a circular orbit of radius r experiences the centripetal force balanced by the attractive ____ force between electron and proton (nucleus).
e: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r toward the centre. It changes the direction of velocity, not the speed, when speed is constant. An electron of charge e and mass m moving in a circular orbit of radius r experiences the centripetal force balanced by the attractive Coulomb force between electron and proton (nucleus).

q: According to the Bohr's postulate II, L=mvr=____.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. According to the Bohr's postulate II, L=mvr=nh/2π.

q: The total energy of hydrogen atom is E=kinetic energy KE + ____ energy PE.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The total energy of hydrogen atom is E=kinetic energy KE + potential energy PE.

q: According to Eq.(12.4), all the energy values are ____ which means electron is bound to the nucleus.
e: According to Eq.(12.4), all the energy values are negative which means electron is bound to the nucleus. Negative is what this statement is using.

q: Here we would introduce an important constant, which is fine structure constant ____ (a dimensionless constant).
e: Here we would introduce an important constant, which is fine structure constant α (a dimensionless constant). Α is what this statement is using.

q: The ground state energy of hydrogen atom is ____ eV.
e: The ground state energy of hydrogen atom is -13.6 eV. -13.6 is what this statement is using.

q: Energy of hydrogen atom in the nth state E = ____ eV (n=1, 2, 3, ...).
e: Energy of hydrogen atom in the nth state E = -13.6/n² eV (n=1, 2, 3,.). Leave the relation as -13.6/n².

q: Radius of hydrogen atom r = ____ $n^2$ Å.
e: Radius of hydrogen atom r = 0.52896 n² Å. 0.52896 is what this statement is using.

q: For n=1, the radius of hydrogen atom is called Bohr's ____(rB), r = 0.52896 Å.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. For n=1, the radius of hydrogen atom is called Bohr's radius(rB), r = 0.52896 Å.

q: A hydrogen discharge tube is a slim tube containing hydrogen gas at ____ pressure with an electrode at each end.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. A hydrogen discharge tube is a slim tube containing hydrogen gas at low pressure with an electrode at each end.

q: If a high voltage is applied, the tube lights up with a bright ____ glow.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. If a high voltage is applied, the tube lights up with a bright pink glow.

q: Bohr's model explains the spectral lines of the hydrogen atomic ____ spectrum.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. Bohr's model explains the spectral lines of the hydrogen atomic emission spectrum.

q: When the atom gains energy, the electron jumps from the ground state to another state with ____ energy.
e: When the atom gains energy, the electron jumps from the ground state to another state with higher energy. Higher is what this statement is using.

q: Energy levels are designated with an integer n which is called principal ____ number.
e: Energy levels are designated with an integer n which is called principal quantum number. The name used here is quantum.

q: The ground state is ____, the first excited state is n=2, and so on.
e: The ground state is n=1, the first excited state is n=2, and so on. Leave the relation as n=1.

q: The energy gained by the atom is equal to the ____ in energy between the two energy levels.
e: The energy gained by the atom is equal to the difference in energy between the two energy levels. Difference is what this statement is using.

q: When the electron returns back from the higher energy state to a lower energy state, it releases energy that is equal to the difference in energy of the two ____.
e: When the electron returns back from the higher energy state to a lower energy state, it releases energy that is equal to the difference in energy of the two orbits. Orbits is what this statement is using.

q: The energy ΔE is released in the form of an electromagnetic radiation with ____.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. The energy ΔE is released in the form of an electromagnetic radiation with frequency v.

q: Radiated energy ΔE = hv = hc/λ = ____ - En_f, and n_i > n_f.
e: Radiated energy ΔE = hv = hc/λ = En_i - En_f, and n_i > n_f. En_i is what this statement is using.

q: As the energy increases further and further from the nucleus, the spacing between the levels gets ____ and ____.
e: As the energy increases further and further from the nucleus, the spacing between the levels gets smaller and ____. Smaller is what this statement is using.

q: In the emission of X-rays, the energy emitted due to electron transition from n=2 energy state to n=1 energy state is ____ characteristic X-rays.
e: In the emission of X-rays, the energy emitted due to electron transition from n=2 energy state to n=1 energy state is K_α characteristic X-rays. K_α is what this statement is using.

q: whereas a transition from n=3 energy state to n=1 energy state is ____ characteristic X-rays.
e: Whereas a transition from n=3 energy state to n=1 energy state is K_β characteristic X-rays. K_β is what this statement is using.

q: When electromagnetic radiation(e.g.light) of sufficient energy incident on the metal surface the ____ are ejected from its surface.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. When electromagnetic radiation(e.g.light) of sufficient energy incident on the metal surface the electrons are ejected from its surface.

q: This phenomenon is known as ____ effect.
e: This phenomenon is known as photoelectric effect. The name used here is photoelectric.

q: These ejected electrons are called ____.
e: These ejected electrons are called photoelectrons. The name used here is photoelectrons.

q: There are no electrons emitted below a certain frequency of incident light which is different for different ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. There are no electrons emitted below a certain frequency of incident light which is different for different metals.

q: This frequency is called the ____ frequency $v_0$.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. This frequency is called the threshold frequency v_0.

q: Photoelectric current is directly proportional to ____ of the incident light.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. Photoelectric current is directly proportional to intensity of the incident light.

q: The kinetic energy of photoelectrons is directly proportional to ____ of the incident light.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The kinetic energy of photoelectrons is directly proportional to frequency of the incident light.

q: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by considering light as a ____.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by considering light as a wave.

q: However, this phenomenon can be explained by the ____ nature of light, in which light can be visualized as a stream of particles of electromagnetic energy.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. However, this phenomenon can be explained by the particle nature of light, in which light can be visualized as a stream of particles of electromagnetic energy.

q: These particles are called ____.
e: These particles are called photons. The name used here is photons.

q: The energy of a photon is related to the frequency of light as, E=____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The energy of a photon is related to the frequency of light as, E=hv.

q: where E is the energy of the photon, h is ____ constant, v is the frequency of light, c is the speed of light (in a vacuum) and λ is the wavelength of the light.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. Where E is the energy of the photon, h is Planck's constant, v is the frequency of light, c is the speed of light (in a vacuum) and λ is the wavelength of the light.

q: The above relation is known as ____ equation.
e: The above relation is known as Planck's equation. The name used here is Planck's.

q: The most important consequence of photoelectric effect leads to the concept of wave-particle ____ nature of either particles or waves.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The most important consequence of photoelectric effect leads to the concept of wave-particle dual nature of either particles or waves.

q: That means light behaves sometimes as a particle and the other times behaves like a ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. That means light behaves sometimes as a particle and the other times behaves like a wave.

q: Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different ____.
e: Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different masses. Masses is what this statement is using.

q: That is, they have the same number of protons but have different number of ____.
e: That is, they have the same number of protons but have different number of neutrons. Neutrons is what this statement is using.

q: In other words, isotopes have the same atomic number but have different ____ number.
e: In other words, isotopes have the same atomic number but have different mass number. Mass is what this statement is using.

q: Since isotopes of an element have same number of electrons, they have same electron configuration and thereby have the same ____ properties.
e: Since isotopes of an element have same number of electrons, they have same electron configuration and thereby have the same chemical properties. Chemical is what this statement is using.

q: They have different ____ properties as they vary in their atomic mass.
e: They have different physical properties as they vary in their atomic mass. Physical is what this statement is using.

q: Some isotopes are ____, that is, they do not decay (or transform) into other elements.
e: Some isotopes are stable, that is, they do not decay (or transform) into other elements. Stable is what this statement is using.

q: However, some are unstable (or ____), that is, decay into other elements.
e: However, some are unstable (or radioactive), that is, decay into other elements. Radioactive is what this statement is using.

q: Stable isotopes and some radioactive isotopes (____) exist naturally.
e: Stable isotopes and some radioactive isotopes (radioisotopes) exist naturally. Radioisotopes is what this statement is using.

q: Isotopes can also be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and particle ____.
e: Isotopes can also be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and particle accelerators. Accelerators is what this statement is using.

q: Every chemical element has one or more ____.
e: Every chemical element has one or more isotopes. Isotopes is what this statement is using.

q: For example, copper has two stable isotopes: ____ and $^{65}\text{Cu}$.
e: For example, copper has two stable isotopes: ^63Cu and ^65Cu. ^63cu is what this statement is using.

q: Three isotopes of hydrogen are: 1H (hydrogen), 2H(deuterium), and 3H(____).
e: Three isotopes of hydrogen are: 1H (hydrogen), 2H(deuterium), and 3H(tritium). Tritium is what this statement is using.

q: Tritium is ____. It transforms into helium isotope 3He.
e: Tritium is radioactive. It transforms into helium isotope 3He. Radioactive is what this statement is using.

q: Of over 1000 isotopes known thus far, the most abundant one in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope ____.
e: Of over 1000 isotopes known thus far, the most abundant one in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope ^1H. ^1h is what this statement is using.

q: In studying cosmology, we get the information of celestial objects by the ____ they emit.
e: In studying cosmology, we get the information of celestial objects by the light they emit. Light is what this statement is using.

q: Their wavelengths are measured to obtain the astronomical ____.
e: Their wavelengths are measured to obtain the astronomical spectra. Spectra is what this statement is using.

q: When a source of light waves is travelling away from the observer, the observed wavelength will be slightly ____ than the wavelength of the stationary (rest) source.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. When a source of light waves is travelling away from the observer, the observed wavelength will be slightly longer than the wavelength of the stationary (rest) source.

q: In astronomy, this shift toward longer wavelengths is referred to as a ____ since red is at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum.
e: In astronomy, this shift toward longer wavelengths is referred to as a redshift since red is at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum. Redshift is what this statement is using.

q: Conversely, a shift toward shorter wavelength, which occurs when the source is moving toward the observer, is called a ____.
e: Conversely, a shift toward shorter wavelength, which occurs when the source is moving toward the observer, is called a blueshift. The name used here is blueshift.

q: The main reasons for redshift are as follows: ____ effect i.e., the movement of objects either closer or apart from each other in space.
e: The main reasons for redshift are as follows: Doppler effect i.e., the movement of objects either closer or apart from each other in space. Doppler is what this statement is using.

q: Strong gravitational force leads to gravitational ____.
e: Strong gravitational force leads to gravitational redshift. Redshift is what this statement is using.

q: Cosmological redshift is such that light stretches (longer wavelength) as space ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Cosmological redshift is such that light stretches (longer wavelength) as space expands.

q: In 1929, ____ examined a series of velocity measurements for different galaxies.
e: In 1929, Edwin Hubble examined a series of velocity measurements for different galaxies. Edwin hubble is what this statement is using.

q: He noticed that the farther away the galaxy the faster it moved, and that the relationship was ____.
e: He noticed that the farther away the galaxy the faster it moved, and that the relationship was linear. Linear is what this statement is using.

q: This relationship between the velocity of a galaxy and its distance has come to be known as the ____ law.
e: This relationship between the velocity of a galaxy and its distance has come to be known as the Hubble law. The name used here is Hubble.

q: It provided the first evidence that the Universe is ____, a result that was rather startling at that time, as it had long been assumed that the Universe was static and unchanging.
e: It provided the first evidence that the Universe is expanding, a result that was rather startling at that time, as it had long been assumed that the Universe was static and unchanging. Expanding is what this statement is using.

q: Hubble's law formula is given as follows: v = ____.
e: Hubble's law formula is given as follows: v = H_0 d. H_0 d is what this statement is using.

q: where v is the velocity of the galaxy in km s^-1, H0 is the Hubble ____ in km s^-1 (Mpc)^-1, d is the distance between the observer and the galaxy in Mpc.
e: Where v is the velocity of the galaxy in km s^-1, H0 is the Hubble constant in km s^-1 (Mpc)^-1, d is the distance between the observer and the galaxy in Mpc. Constant is what this statement is using.

q: Because of the intrinsic motion of galaxies, observed ____ gets influenced.
e: Because of the intrinsic motion of galaxies, observed velocity gets influenced. Velocity is what this statement is using.

q: Galaxy orbiting due to gravitational ____.
e: Galaxy orbiting due to gravitational movements. Movements is what this statement is using.

q: Hubble constant is defined as the unit of measurement, which is used for describing the ____ of the universe.
e: Hubble constant is defined as the unit of measurement, which is used for describing the expansion of the universe. The unit written here is expansion.

q: Hubble constant is ____ km s^-1 (Mpc)^-1.
e: Hubble constant is 72 km s^-1 (Mpc)^-1. 72 is what this statement is using.

q: The redshift formula is given as, z = ____.
e: The redshift formula is given as, z = v/c. Leave the relation as v/c.

q: where z is the redshift, Δλ is the shift in wavelength in the spectra, λ is the wavelength, v is the ____ velocity of space object, c is the speed of light.
e: In vacuum the speed of light is about 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Where z is the redshift, Δλ is the shift in wavelength in the spectra, λ is the wavelength, v is the recession velocity of space object, c is the speed of light.

q: The Hubble time or age of the universe is defined as the ____ of the Hubble constant.
e: The Hubble time or age of the universe is defined as the reciprocal of the Hubble constant. Reciprocal is what this statement is using.

q: Hubble time is given as follows: tH = ____.
e: Hubble time is given as follows: tH = 1/H_0. Leave the relation as 1/H_0.

q: t = ____ years.
e: T = 1.36× 10^10 years. Leave the relation as 1.36× 10^10.

q: t = ____ billion years.
e: T = 13.6 billion years. 13.6 is what this statement is using.

q: The Hubble length is defined as the product of the speed of light and the Hubble ____.
e: In vacuum the speed of light is about 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. The Hubble length is defined as the product of the speed of light and the Hubble time.

q: It is also known as the Hubble ____.
e: It is also known as the Hubble distance. The name used here is distance.

q: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of the ____ universe (visible universe).
e: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of the observable universe (visible universe). Observable is what this statement is using.

q: It is also defined as the volume of sphere whose radius is ____.
e: It is also defined as the volume of sphere whose radius is cH_0^-1. Ch_0^-1 is what this statement is using.
